verses.text: Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, including how he'd killed all the prophets with the sword.
Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah: “May the gods punish me severely if by this time tomorrow I haven't made your life end like theirs!”
When Elijah saw what was happening, he ran for his life. When he reached Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there.
Elijah went a day's journey into the wilderness alone and sat down under a juniper tree. He asked to die. “I've had enough, LORD,” he said. “Take my life. I'm no better than my ancestors.”
He lay down under the juniper tree and fell asleep. An angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
He looked and saw a loaf baked on hot coals and a jar of water beside his head. He ate and drank, then lay down again.
The angel of the LORD came back, touched him, and said, “Get up and eat. The journey ahead is too much for you.”
Elijah got up, ate, and drank. That food gave him strength to travel forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
He found a cave there and stayed in it. The LORD spoke to him and asked, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

Elijah said, “I've been deeply devoted to the LORD, the God of Armies. But the Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I'm the only one left, and now they're trying to kill me too.”

The LORD said, “Go outside and stand on the mountain before the LORD.” As the LORD passed by, a mighty wind tore through the mountains and shattered rocks before him. The LORD wasn't in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the LORD wasn't in the earthquake.
After the earthquake came a fire, but the LORD wasn't in the fire. After the fire came a quiet, gentle voice.
When Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his cloak and went out to stand at the mouth of the cave. A voice asked him, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

Elijah said, “I've been deeply devoted to the LORD, the God of Armies. But the Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I'm the only one left, and now they're trying to kill me too.”
The LORD told him, “Go back the way you came, to the wilderness of Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as king over Syria.
Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel Meholah to take your place as prophet.
Anyone who escapes Hazael's sword will be killed by Jehu, and anyone who escapes Jehu's sword will be killed by Elisha.
But I've kept seven thousand people in Israel, every one whose knees have never bowed to Baal and whose lips have never kissed him.”
Elijah left and found Elisha son of Shaphat plowing with twelve teams of oxen. Elisha was working the twelfth team. Elijah went over and put his cloak on him.
Elisha left his oxen and ran after Elijah. “Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I'll follow you.” Elijah said, “Go back. What have I done to you?”
Elisha went back, killed his team of oxen, and used their equipment to cook the meat. He gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he got up, followed Elijah, and became his attendant.
